=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer-side assessment

The Seller’s package is not balanced for Wattlebridge as drafted. It combines broad liability protections and generic disclosure with unresolved transaction risks that could affect control of the business, title to important IP, completion funding and post-completion liabilities. The key pushbacks are below. This is a commercial issue-spotting review based on the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter; the complete SPA, schedules, due diligence record and funds flow should be checked before settling drafting.

### 1. Liability limits and claim mechanics

- **General cap of AUD 4.8 million (20% of price): push back.** It may be inadequate for the risk profile, particularly if several material issues arise together. Seek a materially higher cap, or separate caps for different risk categories, and ensure the cap applies only to general warranty claims—not title, capacity, tax, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **De minimis and tipping basket: push back.** A AUD 25,000 per-claim threshold and AUD 250,000 basket that allows recovery only above the basket shift meaningful loss to Buyer. Seek a lower de minimis and a **deductible basket** (once crossed, recovery from dollar one), or no basket for material or specific claims. Clarify aggregation of related claims and prevent artificial fragmentation.
- **18-month warranty period: likely too short.** Seek a longer period for general warranties and longer, appropriately tailored periods for tax and other claims that may emerge later. Fundamental warranties should not share the general-warranty cap or time limit. Consider requiring notice of a claim within the period, with the claim then surviving until resolved.
- **“All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise”: reject.** This risks extending caps, thresholds, time bars and other restrictions to claims that should be treated differently. State expressly which limitations apply to which claims, and carve out fraud and deliberate concealment, title/capacity, tax claims and negotiated specific indemnities as appropriate.
- **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to all claims: reject or narrow substantially.** Those provisions should not inadvertently bar claims for fraud, deliberate concealment, breach of specific covenants or indemnities, or other expressly preserved rights. Any exclusive-remedy provision should preserve agreed indemnities and enforcement of completion obligations. The non-reliance clause should not negate express contractual warranties or remedies.

### 2. Overbroad disclosure and buyer-knowledge protections

- **General disclosure of the entire data room and public records: reject.** It makes it difficult to identify what the Seller says qualifies each warranty and risks turning a large, indexed repository into blanket protection. Require **fair, specific disclosure** in the letter, with enough detail to identify the nature, scope and relevance of the matter. Limit any data-room reference to identified documents, and agree a fixed, preserved version of the room.
- **Public-register disclosure: narrow.** Public availability is not the same as fair disclosure to Buyer. If retained, identify the relevant record and its significance; do not deem all searchable records disclosed.
- **Buyer-knowledge exclusion: reject in its present form.** Knowledge of advisers, or matters that could have been found through diligence or public searches, is too broad and uncertain. At most, agree a tightly defined exclusion for actual, specific knowledge of named Buyer representatives, without constructive or imputed knowledge, and do not let it override express warranties or specific indemnities.
- **The letter’s reservation that it admits no breach, liability, materiality or required action:** unsurprising as a reservation, but it does not resolve the underlying risks. Do not accept the Seller’s characterisation of a disclosed issue as harmless merely because the letter disclaims conclusions. Require the SPA and completion documents to allocate the risk.

### 3. Conditions, debt and completion mechanics

- **Bluefen consent: do not treat a written consent alone as satisfaction.** Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. The disclosure says no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions is included. Make effective, unconditional consent—and satisfaction or waiver of all associated conditions—a condition precedent to completion. “Reasonable endeavours” is not an adequate substitute for an outcome on this key customer. Include a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right if the condition is not met.
- **Riverlark debt and security: completion release, not a post-completion promise.** The AUD 3.2 million facility is outstanding and no final discharge is in the room. For a debt-free/cash-free deal, require repayment at completion from agreed funds flow, delivery of lender payout and release documents, and discharge of all security (including releases effective against the relevant registers). Do not accept a release merely to be provided after completion. Verify whether any break fees, accrued interest or other amounts affect price or funds flow.
- **Completion funds flow: reconcile it to the AUD 24 million price and agreed debt-free/cash-free mechanics.** Obtain an itemised, agreed funds flow showing purchase price, debt repayment, cash, transaction expenses, adjustments and all other completion payments. The Seller’s statement that the flow reflects agreed mechanics is not a substitute for checking it.

### 4. Specific identified exposures

- **Employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 is omitted from the funds flow.** The bonuses are conditional on completion and continued employment, and payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. Establish who bears the bonuses and on-costs. Buyer’s preferred position is that all amounts arising from pre-completion arrangements are either reflected as a debt-like item or paid by Seller at or before completion, with appropriate tax/on-cost treatment and no double counting. Confirm whether the continued-employment condition creates post-completion obligations for Buyer.
- **Ironquay IP: the existing indemnity appears too narrow.** The disclosed contract makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 is open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Require evidence of cleared payment and an effective assignment/transfer of all required materials and IP at or before completion, with any necessary consents and moral-rights arrangements. Seek a specific indemnity for loss arising from non-payment, non-transfer, infringement or third-party claims—not merely the stated SOW3 payment. Do not rely on the Seller’s characterisation of the existing indemnity as adequate without reviewing its exact scope and survival.
- **Export/privacy incident: not safely dismissed as preliminary or immaterial.** The disclosure describes an unintended external-email download link and potentially 1,240 records, while access, scope and notification obligations remain unverified. Require the investigation and remediation to be completed or properly documented, relevant records and regulator/customer communications disclosed, and any required notifications made. Seek a specific indemnity for pre-completion incident liabilities and costs, plus suitable warranties and a closing update. Preserve Buyer’s ability to assess completion or seek a remedy if material facts emerge.
- **Supplier renewals: AUD 330,000 needs investigation and allocation.** The records must be read together, and do not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. Obtain each contract, renewal date, termination rights and accrued amounts. Ensure accrued/pre-completion liabilities are captured in the accounts or completion adjustment, and consider a debt-like adjustment or specific protection for unavoidable commitments not reflected in the agreed price. Do not accept “ordinary-course operating costs” without evidence.
- **Office lease and Mossvale:** the letter does not establish that consent is required for a share sale; equally, it does not establish that no action is needed. Review the actual lease and contract wording, notice requirements, assignment language and any control-change provisions. Require any required notice/consent or waiver before completion, and a warranty that no other consent or default is triggered. Avoid asserting a consent condition unless the contract supports it.
- **Title:** DD-012 is a source, not independent verification. Require customary title and capacity warranties that Seller owns and can transfer 100% of the shares free of encumbrances, confirm issued capital and options/convertibles, and deliver executed transfer documents and updated statutory registers at completion. These warranties should have a suitably high or uncapped negotiated protection and should not be reduced to the general cap/time bar.

### 5. Tax and IP warranties

The Seller’s assertion that tax and IP are “settled” under the general regime is not a substitute for agreed protections. Tax risk may emerge well after 18 months, and the Ironquay issue shows a concrete chain-of-title concern. Seek tailored tax and IP warranties, appropriate survival periods and caps, and specific indemnities for identified pre-completion exposures. Ensure any tax indemnity is not neutralised by the general cap, basket, exclusive-remedy clause or disclosure wording.

## Summary of recommendations

Prioritise these points in the mark-up and negotiations:

1. **Narrow general disclosure and delete or tightly define the buyer-knowledge bar.**
2. **Separate liability regimes:** improve the general cap/basket/time period, and carve out or separately protect title, capacity, tax, fraud and specific indemnities.
3. **Make Bluefen consent and its associated conditions a genuine condition precedent.**
4. **Require Riverlark repayment and effective security release at completion.**
5. **Reconcile the funds flow, explicitly addressing the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs.**
6. **Resolve Ironquay IP transfer and payment, and obtain stronger specific protection.**
7. **Investigate and allocate the export incident and supplier-renewal exposure rather than accepting the Seller’s low-risk labels.**
8. **Verify all relevant change-control, notice and title matters against the underlying contracts and registers.**

The central negotiating principle is to avoid letting broad disclosure and generic limitations defeat the express risk allocation in the SPA. For each identified issue, obtain evidence, a completion deliverable or a tailored indemnity—and ensure the liability regime preserves the remedy.
